look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · UNARMED scrambling or climbing nightshade with often LOBED ovate leaves, PURPLE corolla lobes strongly REFLEXED backward, a close-packed yellow ANTHER CONE, and clusters of shiny RED berries. Flower clusters commonly much branched with 7–40 flowers. Leaf basal lobes, anther arrangement and cluster branching are better together than berry color alone. RARE WHITE-flowered bittersweet exists. Texas nightshade (S. triquetrum) can also scramble and make red fruit, but generally has smaller white flowers, more individually distinct yellow anthers, sharply triangular/hastate leaves and 3–6-flowered clusters. Do NOT eat berries; introduced comparison, not a locally certified native.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: UNARMED woody or herbaceous SCRAMBLING vine-like perennial (not a true tendril vine); older stems can persist.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: ALTERNATE petiolate leaves usually ovate/heart-shaped, often with one or two pointed SIDE LOBES near base; some leaves entirely unlobed.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: 5-part DEEPLY REFLEXED purple/violet petals (rare WHITE); shiny GREEN/WHITE markings near petal bases may be visible in larger macros, not reliably visible in existing photo.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: Yellow anthers 4.5–6 mm (Flora of North America), held CONNIVENT/clustered into a compact cone; never call them 'fused' solely from ordinary photos.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: Many-branched, often 7–40-flowered clusters; pedicels insert into small sleeves on axis. Flowers roughly 1.5–2 cm wide.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: Shiny red mature berries roughly 0.5–1.5 cm long and green/purplish five-lobed calyces at base, as visible in current exact-species fruit photograph.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: FNA lists introduced-range occurrence widely in North America. Preserve this project's COMPARISON_NONNATIVE native-metrics exclusion.

lookalikes.differences: SOLANUM DULCAMARA vs TEXAS NIGHTSHADE: purple REFLEXED corolla and tightly CONNIVENT yellow anthers, many-branched 7–40-flower clusters, ovate to basally lobed leaves versus usually small WHITE flowers with more separate FREE anthers, 3–6-flowered clusters, sharply triangular/hastate leaves and more angular stems. Exceptions: white-flowered S. dulcamara; both make red fruit, both scramble.
